claim: Replicative DNA polymerases alone are distributive, synthesizing very few nucleotides of complementary DNA before disengaging from an elongating primer strand.
source: Replicative DNA polymerases (pols) alone are distributive, synthesizing very few nucleotides of complementary DNA before disengaging from an elongating primer strand.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about DNA polymerases.

claim: Replicative polymerases anchor to ring-shaped sliding clamps to achieve high processivity required for efficient DNA replication.
source: To achieve the high processivity required for efficient DNA replication, replicative pols anchor to ring-shaped sliding clamps, forming the holoenzyme.
evidence: This is established knowledge about DNA replication mechanisms.

claim: Sliding clamps are dimers or trimers of identical subunits aligned head-to-tail, forming a toroidal structure.
source: Sliding clamps are dimers or trimers of identical subunits aligned head-to-tail, forming a highly-conserved, toroidal structure with two structurally distinct faces and a central cavity large enough to encircle double-stranded DNA and slide freely along it.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about sliding clamps.

claim: The C-terminal face of sliding clamps serves as a platform for interaction with replicative polymerases.
source: The 'C-terminal face' contains all C-termini and serves as a platform for interaction with replicative pols (Hedglin et al., in press; Yao and O'Donnell, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other scientific work.

claim: Most sliding clamps are closed in solution.
source: In solution, most sliding clamps are closed, requiring an enzyme-catalyzed mechanism which; (1) disrupts an interface within the sliding clamp ring and holds it open for assembly
evidence: This is supported by citations to other scientific work.

claim: Clamp loaders are heteropentameric complexes that utilize ATP to catalyze site-directed loading of sliding clamps onto DNA.
source: Such feats are achieved by heteropentameric complexes referred to as clamp loaders, which utilize ATP to catalyze site-directed loading of sliding clamps onto DNA.
evidence: This is established knowledge about clamp loader function.

claim: Clamp loaders are composed of two to five distinct subunits that assemble into a tight heteropentameric complex.
source: Clamp loaders are composed of two to five distinct subunits that assemble into a tight heteropentameric complex with an overall structure that is conserved throughout evolution.
evidence: This is established knowledge about clamp loader structure.

claim: Each clamp loader subunit belongs to the AAA+ superfamily of ATPases.
source: Each subunit belongs to the AAA+ superfamily of ATPases that contain characteristic ATP-binding/hydrolysis motifs that convert the energy from ATP binding and hydrolysis to mechanical force.
evidence: This is established knowledge about clamp loader subunit classification.

claim: In the presence of ATP, clamp loaders bind the C-terminal face of their respective clamp and open it for assembly.
source: In the presence of ATP, clamp loaders bind the C-terminal face of their respective clamp and open it for assembly.
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: The open clamp•clamp loader complex binds a P/T junction, adopting a 'notched screw cap arrangement' that matches the helical geometry of the DNA duplex.
source: Once formed, the open clamp•clamp loader complex binds a P/T junction, adopting a 'notched screw cap arrangement' that matches the helical geometry of the DNA duplex (Simonetta et al., 2009; Kelch et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: ATP hydrolysis is optimized in the notched screw cap arrangement.
source: In this orientation, ATP hydrolysis is optimized and the clamp loader reverts to a low-affinity DNA-binding state upon hydrolysis of ATP and ejects from the P/T junction, leaving behind the loaded clamp.
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: The clamp loader ejects from the P/T junction upon ATP hydrolysis, leaving behind the loaded clamp.

evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.
